1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees,
tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are recorded cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no. 42/4(4 16), 7 min (004), 14 min (206), 15 (416), 17 min (319) and 41/6(416) total land measuring 20 bigha and 17 biswas (in short, the said land) having share as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.
5.
It is stated that the petitioners are only persons entitled to receive the compensation amount as per the actual prevailing market rate of the said land.
The actual physical possession of the said land has not been taken till the filing of the petitioner.

It is stated that the said award is not acceptable and the Award amount has been received under protest and without LAC no. 291 / 2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Puran Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 prejudice to their rights.

sentences.text: There is one Badberi Tree aged about two years and one boring in the said.
The petitioners have spent more than Rs. 20,000 on it.
The trees weigh more than 5 quintals and the rate of wood is @ Rs. 500 per quintal.

6. It is stated that the petitioners has levelled the said land throughout having means of irrigation and were reaping three healthy crops in a year including the seasonal vegetables in between and the cattle feeds and were earning about Rs. 1 lakh per acre per year from selling the agricultural produce after retaining them for their domestic use.

The said land is surrounded by the well developed the areas having all basic modern facilities i.e. well connected roads, adequate transport facility,
hospitals, schools, colleges, reputed clubs, farmhouses, party lawns and banquet Halls and is,
therefore, having the market value @ Rs. 8000 per square yards and the agricultural land was sold at this rate in the surrounding areas.

The NH 10 is 2 kms away from the said land, the bottling plant of Indian Gas and FCI godown is around 3 kms from the said land, and Mundka, Udyog Vihar,
metro workstation is around 2 kms from the said land, Railway Station Mundka and other developed areas having all the transport facilities and basic amenities
are around 1 kms from the said land.
7. The said land is also covered in master plan and is to be treated as "developed one" or all purposes.
These factors leads to inescapable conclusion that the said land be valued @ Rs. 8000 per square yards.

It is also submitted that ld. LAC failed to appreciate that it is the distance and the potentiality of the land and not the village, which is to be kept in mind while awarding the compensation.

It is stated that the ld.

sentences.text: It is stated that the respondent no.2

has allotted the adjoining land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000 per square yards and that too only to hose who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which shows that that the land for residential and commercial purposes was not so easily available @ Rs. 6000 per square yards.

The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped the land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/turn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioners.
11. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money and the ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioners.
The ld. LAC has grossly erred in deducting the tax, as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it is interalia submitted that the present petition is not maintainable as the petitioner have failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the petition.
The market value of the said land has already been assessed by the ld. LAC by taking into consideration the prevailing market rates.

All the other contents of the petition were denied in toto and it is submitted that the reference petition is based on false and frivolous grounds and as such the same may be dismissed and the petitioners are not entitled to any enhancement of compensation.

13. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award relating to village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the said land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

14. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The LAC no.
291 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Puran Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

sentences.text: It is stated that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
15. It is submitted that the possession of the land has been handed over to the DDA on 06.09.2005 and after taking possession same was transferred to RPDVII on 16.09.2005.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation

,

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
18. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT?
OPP 19.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the LAC no. 291 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Puran Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

sentences.text:
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
20.

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Ram Kishan (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
21. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

22. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same LAC no. 291 /
2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Puran Singh & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.

There is no evidence on record to gather Sh. Puran Singh vs Union Of India on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73162259/

24. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
